item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
641
ABPZ20 KNHC 091142
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Fri Oct 9 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles west of the southern tip
of the Baja California Peninsula, and on Hurricane Simon, located a
couple of hundred miles south of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions are expected to
be conducive for some gradual development thereafter, and a tropical
depression could form as the system moves generally
west-northwestward at around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 49
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 090856
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  49
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...RACHEL WEAKENS SLIGHTLY NOW ON A NORTHEASTWARD TRACK...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...22.7N 124.9W
ABOUT 955 MI...1535 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 840 MI...1350 KM SW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...50 MPH...85 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 45 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...994 MB...29.36 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in extreme northern Baja California, northern Gulf of 
California, and Southern California should monitor the progress of 
Rachel. Tropical Storm Watches will be likely be required for a 
portion of this area later today.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 22.7 North, longitude 124.9 West. Rachel is
moving toward the northeast near 3 mph (6 km/h). This general motion 
is expected to continue, with a significant increase in forward 
speed over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast during the next 48 hours. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles (165 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 994 mb (29.36 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header
WTPZ43 KNHC.

WIND: The risk of tropical-storm-force winds is increasing for 
portions of northern Baja California through extreme northwestern 
Mexico this weekend, and a Tropical Storm Watch may be required for 
a portion of that area later today. Strong gusty winds associated 
with the system are expected to spread over interior portions of the 
Southwest United States, especially in areas of higher terrain, from 
this weekend into early next week.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of
Baja California this weekend.
 
Rachel and associated moisture of the system will also bring
rainfall of 1 to 3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5
inches in portions of the Southwest United States this weekend. This
will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for flash
and urban flooding.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall
Graphic available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and
the Flash Flood Risk graphic at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Swells partly generated by Rachel will build along the coast
of Southern California and northern Baja California through the
weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions as well as minor to moderate coastal
flooding. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 49
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 090857
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  49
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM PDT Fri Oct 09 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Rachel's convective organization 
remains limited, with the deepest convection confined to the 
northern semicircle. The latest subjective Dvorak intensity 
estimate from TAFB was T3.0/45 kt, which is in good agreement with 
the latest objective estimates from UW-CIMSS. Given these data and 
the limited convective organization, the initial intensity is 
lowered to 45 kt.

Rachel has begun its anticipated northeastward turn over the past
several hours, with an initial motion estimated at 045/3 kt. A
northeastward motion with a significant increase in forward speed
is expected during the next couple of days as the cyclone
interacts with a deepening mid- to upper-level trough over the
western United States. Track guidance remains in good agreement
and depicts Rachel moving ashore over the northern Baja California
Peninsula late Saturday before continuing northeastward into the
southwestern United States on Sunday. The latest NHC track
forecast is largely unchanged from the previous prediction and
lies close to the HCCA and GDMI aids.

Despite the very dry and stable air and relatively cool sea surface 
temperatures along the forecast track, some of the dynamical 
guidance suggests that Rachel could maintain tropical storm strength 
through landfall this weekend. As Rachel accelerates northeastward 
and interacts with the deepening trough, increasing upper-level 
forcing and improving mid-level moisture could support intermittent 
bursts of deep convection. Although this interaction will also 
result in a significant increase in vertical wind shear, which 
should further disrupt the cyclone's tropical structure, some 
strengthening is possible during the next 24 to 36 hours. The latest 
NHC intensity forecast shows Rachel reaching 50 kt in 36 h before 
weakening as it moves inland. Rachel is expected to become 
post-tropical over the southwestern United States by 60 h and 
dissipate shortly thereafter. The latest NHC intensity forecast is 
similar to the previous prediction and lies near the middle to upper 
end of the guidance envelope. Given the potential for 
tropical-storm-force winds along portions of northern Baja 
California this weekend, a Tropical Storm Watch will likely be 
required for portions of the northern Baja California Peninsula 
will be likely later today.
 
 
Key Messages:

1. Rachel is expected to approach the coast of northern Baja 
California, Mexico, and the northern Gulf of California at tropical 
storm strength over the weekend, and a Tropical Storm Watch could 
be required for a portion of this area later today.

2. Strong gusty winds associated with the remnants of Rachel are
expected to spread over interior portions of the Southwest United
States, especially in areas of higher terrain, from this weekend
into early next week.

3. Rachel and the moisture associated with the system will spread
over portions of the Southwest United States and northern Baja
California Peninsula through this weekend. This will lead to
increasing coverage of rainfall and the potential for flash and
urban flooding.

4. Swells partly generated by Rachel will continue to build along
the coast of Southern California and northern Baja California.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions, as well as minor to moderate coastal flooding,
through early next week. Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  09/0900Z 22.7N 124.9W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  09/1800Z 23.0N 124.4W   40 KT  45 MPH
 24H  10/0600Z 24.1N 122.4W   45 KT  50 MPH
 36H  10/1800Z 26.5N 119.3W   50 KT  60 MPH
 48H  11/0600Z 30.8N 116.5W   45 KT  50 MPH
 60H  11/1800Z 35.3N 114.2W   35 KT  40 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 72H  12/0600Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
966 
WTPZ35 KNHC 091446
TCPEP5
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
...SIMON FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY AND APPROACH THE COAST OF
MEXICO AS A DANGEROUS MAJOR HURRICANE THIS WEEKEND...
...PREPARATIONS SHOULD BE RUSHED TO COMPLETION TODAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.0N 104.7W
ABOUT 210 MI...335 KM S OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 310 MI...500 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 325 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...973 MB...28.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has issued a Hurricane Watch from Punta 
Mita northward to San Blas.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita

A Hurricane Watch is in effect for...
* Punta Mita to San Blas
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued
36 hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion.

A Hurricane Watch means that hurricane conditions are possible
within the watch area.  A watch is typically issued 48 hours
before the anticipated first occurrence of tropical-storm-force
winds, conditions that make outside preparations difficult or
dangerous.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located
near latitude 16.0 North, longitude 104.7 West. Simon is moving
toward the northwest near 3 mph (6 km/h). A slow turn toward the
north is expected today and tonight. Simon is then forecast to move
generally northward, with the center passing very near or over the
west-central coast of Mexico on Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 100 mph (155 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Continued rapid strengthening is expected during 
the next day or so. Simon is forecast to become a major hurricane by 
this evening and strengthen further on Saturday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles
(130 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 973 mb (28.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND:  Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area
Saturday evening or Sunday, with tropical storm conditions expected
Saturday morning.  Tropical storm conditions are possible within
the Tropical Storm Watch area beginning tonight or early Saturday.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 8 to 15
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals of 25 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima,
Jalisco and Nayarit through Sunday.  This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE:  A dangerous storm surge is likely along the
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions.  Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1200 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 090846
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 AM CST Fri Oct 09 2026
 
Simon has quickly strengthened this morning.  A EUMETSAT METOP-B
Microwave Humidity Sounder (MHS) image revealed a small banding eye
feature, and the IR-BD curve enhancement indicates -83C cold cloud
tops associated with a small central dense overcast over the
surface center.  Water vapor imagery and satellite wind data
indicate developing cyclonic outflow above 200 mb.  Based on the
much improved cloud pattern and the TAFB subjective intensity
estimate of T4.5 (77 kt), the initial intensity is increased to 80
kt.
 
Simon's small, intense inner core, favorable environmental 
conditions, low shear, very warm oceanic temperatures, and high 
mid-level moisture content all support a rapid intensification 
event, which appears to be well underway.  Further significant 
strengthening is expected, and the cyclone is forecast to be a very 
dangerous major hurricane when it approaches the coast of Mexico.  
The guidance also shows compact Simon quickly weakening and over the 
high mountainous terrain by early next week.  The NHC forecast is 
once again hedged toward the high end of the guidance, in best 
agreement with the HFIP-HCCA model.
 
Simon's initial motion is estimated to be northwestward, or
315/4 kt.  A northward motion is forecast by early Saturday while 
high pressure over central Mexico weakens and shifts eastward, in 
response to an amplifying mid-tropospheric trough approaching Baja 
California.  The HiRes global models (ECM/GFS/CMC/UKM), HAFS 
hurricane models and the NOAA GEFS AI ensemble mean continue to 
agree more with Simon approaching the west-central coast of Mexico 
on Sunday.  The HCCA and the Google DeepMind ensemble mean have 
been somewhat inconsistent during the past 2 cycles, 
windshield-wipering with a track either inland or just offshore 
beyond the 48-hour period.  Additionally, the along-track forward 
speeds have also become inconsistent, which has slightly affected 
the wind impact timing.  To minimize these track forecast 
inconsistencies, the NHC forecast blends the various consensus aids 
and is nudged to the right of the HCCA and GDM ensemble mean 
solutions.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Simon is expected to approach the west-central coast of Mexico
as a major hurricane on Saturday.
 
2. Life-threatening wind and storm surge impacts are expected along
a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a Hurricane
Warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita.
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed by
late Friday.
 
3. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of 
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall may produce 
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of 
steep terrain.
 
4. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
